title: Man. Post. Cap. V: judicial act; own vs surety; Adam as ours; each own person
pass_a_gloss: Imputation of sin of that kind is a judge's act whereby, by his sentence, he ascribes sin to someone—declaring him guilty of a definite sin and therefore liable to penalty. Sin is ascribed to a person either as to a sinner, or as to one who of his own accord bears the sinner's person as a surety: to the first as his own, to the second as another's. If Adam's actual sin is imputed to us, it is charged not as another's but as ours; yet each of us, when conceived and born, bears his own person, not Adam's, and is not Adam's surety.
pass_b_english: Now such an imputation of sin is the act of a judge ascribing sin to someone by his sentence—that is, pronouncing someone guilty of a certain sin, and therefore to be visited with punishment. But sin is ascribed to someone either as to a sinner, or as to one who voluntarily sustains the sinner's person, as a surety: to the former as his own, to the latter as another's. If Adam's actual sin is imputed to us, it is ascribed not as another's, but as ours: for each of us, when he is conceived and born, bears his own person, not Adam's, whose surety he is not.
source_text: Est autem ejusmodi imputatio peccati, actus judicis sententia sua peccatum alicui tribuentis, hoc est, aliquem certi cujusdam peccati reum esse pronunciantis, ac propterea poena afficiendum. Tribuitur autem alicui peccatum vel tanquam peccatori, vel tanquam peccatoris personam ultro sustinenti, vadi: illi ut suum, huic ut alienum. Nobis si peccatum Adami actuale imputatur, tribuitur, non ut alienum, sed ut nostrum: suam enim quisque nostrum, cum concipitur & nascitur, personam, non Adami, cujus vas non est, gerit.
